title: Anthropic says it will watermark text generated by its AI models
slides: Can you trust any word online anymore?
Anthropic will watermark all AI-generated text
The watermark survives rewriting and copy-paste?
Undetectable changes may still go unnoticed forever
Start auditing your sources before they vanish
thread_text:
1. Who wrote this?

Anthropic's new watermark will tag every AI word, but it can be stripped by rewriting. The question is: who gets blamed when it fails?

2. The invisible mark

The watermark is a statistical pattern, not a visible stamp. It survives copy-paste but not heavy edits. Think of it as a fingerprint that breaks under pressure.

3. The rewriting loophole

Undetectable changes, like swapping synonyms, can erase the mark. So the safeguard only catches lazy copying, not determined cheaters. The blind spot is wide.

4. The vanishing act

If a text is edited, the watermark disappears, and so does the proof. Once the source is gone, you can't verify what was real. The trail ends.

5. Check your own sources

Take a recent AI-generated article and try rewriting one sentence. Does the watermark vanish? If yes, start questioning everything you read today.

instagram.caption:
Every word you read online might soon carry an invisible mark—Anthropic is adding a statistical watermark to all text its models generate. It’s not a visible stamp; it’s a pattern baked into word choices that survives copy-paste.

The catch? Heavy edits, like swapping synonyms, can strip the mark completely. So the system catches lazy copying, not someone who rewrites a sentence by hand.

If you publish AI-assisted content, this changes your liability: a "lightly edited" draft could lose its proof of origin, and readers can’t verify what’s real. Before you share that next AI-generated piece, try rewriting one sentence—if the watermark vanishes, what’s left to trust? 🔍✍️🕵️
